subject: Retention SLAs, backup log access, and next steps (post-demo)
messages:
From: Alex Martin <security@clearhealthit.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up from demo — retention & backups

Sean,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — the product looked promising. A couple of items the compliance team asked me to confirm so we can move to a security questionnaire: 

- What are your standard data retention SLAs for generated content and embeddings? Specifically: primary storage retention, backups, and log retention (API request logs, token-level traces).
- Do you provide a documented deletion confirmation (auditable proof) when a customer requests data erasure? Is that covered in your SOC 2 controls?
- For backups: how long are backups retained, where are they stored (region), and do you maintain separate deletion/retention schedules for backups vs primary store?

Can you also point me to any SOC 2 summary or evidence we can share with our internal auditors? If it’s easier, we can fill out a short questionnaire — happy to start that once we have the above.

Thanks,
Alex Martin
Security Manager
ClearHealth IT

--
Alex Martin
ClearHealth IT | security@clearhealthit.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <security@clearhealthit.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 18:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — retention & backups

Alex — great questions, thanks for sending these. Short answers up front and then I’ll loop in Lauren (solutions) and Priyom (security ops) for the technical evidence.

1) Retention SLAs
- Primary stored outputs (generations & embeddings): configurable retention with defaults at 90 days for hosted accounts; customers can request longer retention on Dedicated/Private. We’ll share the retention matrix.
- Logs (API request metadata, non-sensitive traces): retained 30 days by default; options for extended retention up to 365 days on Dedicated with a retention addon.

2) Deletion confirmation
- Yes — we provide a deletion confirmation with a transaction ID and timestamp. For hosted customers we retain an audit record that deletion ran; for Dedicated/Private customers, proof-of-deletion artifacts can be provided on request.

3) Backups
- Backups: 30-90 day rotation depending on plan. Backups are geo-redundant within the customer-selected cloud region by default. Backups follow a separate retention schedule and are only held for disaster recovery windows, not as an alternative to permanent records.

Attached I’m sending a short SOC 2 summary and a retention matrix (stubs for now). Lauren — can you confirm the log retention extension options and whether we can provide a sanitized sample retention policy for ClearHealth auditors? Priyom — can you advise on the mechanized proof-of-deletion artifacts (KMS/HSM audit notes) we can share?

Next steps: I’ll put together a concise Q&A for you (one-pager) and we can kick off the vendor questionnaire once you confirm which format you prefer (Excel or the online portal).

Best,
Sean
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary, 2pg), backup-retention-matrix.xlsx (matrix stub)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <security@clearhealthit.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — retention & backups

Alex — quick follow-up from my side with the operational details you asked for. I’ll keep this high level and we can hand off more technical artifacts behind an NDA or through your vendor portal.

- Log retention extension: for Dedicated plans we can enable extended log retention up to 365 days. This is configured per-route and billed as an addon. For Hosted accounts we can provide 90-day retention on request (subject to capacity and SSO verification).
- Backup snapshots: nightly snapshots retained for 30 days by default; weekly snapshots retained for 13 weeks; monthly snapshots retained for 12 months ONLY for Dedicated customers who opt into longer DR windows. Snapshots are encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys when in Private/Dedicated.
- Deletion proof: we emit a deletion transaction record (ID + UTC timestamp + object keys affected). For audits we can provide a signed log excerpt (HMAC) showing the deletion took place; full e-discovery packages require an executed DPA addendum.

If you want, I can start filling the questionnaire now — Alex, can you share the vendor questionnaire file or portal link? If you prefer not to share, I’ll prepare the standard security pack and a short appendix documenting backup retention windows by plan.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martin <security@clearhealthit.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — retention & backups

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple clarifications before we proceed: 

- For hosted accounts, you mentioned 90 days default but also "on request" for 90-day retention on logs. Is there a formal SLA or written commitment we can include in the procurement paperwork for our security team?
- For the deletion proof: will the HMAC-signed log excerpt be sufficient as evidence, or do you provide an auditable certificate tied to the SOC 2 controls? Our auditors prefer a signed artifact that references the control ID.
- We have a short vendor questionnaire (attached). Please take a look and let me know if we should put this on the vendor portal instead.

I attached the questionnaire (ClearHealth-Vendor-Questionnaire.xlsx). If you prefer, we can also accept targeted answers in an email Q&A.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — would like to move this to procurement next week if possible.

Alex

Attachments: ClearHealth-Vendor-Questionnaire.xlsx (form)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <security@clearhealthit.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:00:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — retention & backups

Alex — thanks for the questionnaire, we reviewed it and can respond inline. High-level commitments below; Priyom and Lauren will attach the technical artifacts via a secure SharePoint link once we have an NDA in place (I included the HubSpot deal link below for reference).

- Hosted retention SLA: Redwood commits to the configured retention windows described in our retention matrix. For procurement we can add a standard SLA clause: "Retention compliance for hosted accounts will be performed within 7 business days of a valid deletion request; evidence will be provided as a signed deletion record." We can scope tighter SLAs for enterprise purchases (Dedicated/Private).
- Deletion evidence & SOC 2: The HMAC-signed log excerpt maps to SOC 2 control A.3.2 in our summary; we can provide a signed certificate that references the SOC 2 control ID and the deletion transaction ID for audit purposes.
- Backups: Confirmed — default snapshot windows and retention differ by plan. For ClearHealth procurement we recommend Dedicated with 12-month monthly retention if you need long-term backups in-scope for audits.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll upload a short Q&A (answers inline) to a secure SharePoint and share access.
2) Priyom will prepare the HMAC-signed sample excerpt and SOC 2 control reference (requires a short NDA).
3) If that’s acceptable, we’ll prepare a procurement-side SLA addendum for Hosted/Dedicated options.

I’ll follow up early next week with the SharePoint link. Thanks again — looking forward to moving this to the procurement phase.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
